- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly — apply a 1–2 period lag in downward revision.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.1–0.2 per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model often overestimates volatility — cap forecast variance at 0.8x historical range.
